statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 7 with NQ observed at 29,565.00, up 0.09% on the 29,538.75 settle, after a 69-point retracement from the 29,633.75 session high back into the middle of a two-sided 29,489.75-29,633.75 Globex band that is only 0.49% wide. The extreme-hold flagged an hour earlier resolved into mean reversion rather than repeated extension, which removes the single tail amplifier that was present. ES +0.05% in an 18.50-point range and VIX at 15.72 confirm the absence of directional thrust. Stress rises to 77 with Brent through $100.02, WTI at a three-month high and the 10-year at 4.80%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-15:00 UTC, the U.S. cash open and first full hour, where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the most plausible route to repeated extension after failed retracements. A secondary checkpoint sits at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.80% yield coincides with the Apple keynote, and a third at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: NQ retraces 69 points off the 29,633.75 high to 29,565.00 and tail eases to 7, while Brent through $100.02 and a 4.80% 10-year lift stress to 77
body: At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 shows no evidence of mean-reversion failure, and the one amplifier present an hour ago has cleared. NQ futures trade at 29,565.00, up 26.25 points or 0.09% from the 29,538.75 settle, inside a Globex range of 29,489.75-29,633.75. Price marked the 29,633.75 high and then retraced roughly 69 points, about 0.23%, back into the middle of a band that is only 144 points or 0.49% wide. That is precisely the behaviour the reverse/grid approach depends on: the session extreme was rejected rather than held, and the band has now been traded from both sides. Investing.com corroborates the level at 29,565.00 with the same 0.09% change and the same 29,538.75 previous close. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,684.50 are up 0.05% in an 18.50-point range, so the cross-index picture is contained rather than directional. The cash Nasdaq-100 closed the prior session at 29,507.70, down 0.12%, after a two-sided 29,400.70-29,655.73 day, and VIX settled at 15.72, a level inconsistent with a persistent one-way regime. The macro backdrop is what carries stress rather than structure. Brent crude has now printed $100.02, up 2.14% on the day and 14% over the past month, after Houthi attacks halted operations at Saudi energy facilities in the south of the kingdom and amid continuing US-Iran strikes around the Strait of Hormuz; WTI at $94.65 is up 1.74% at a three-month high. The 10-year Treasury yield holds 4.80%, its highest since October 2023, with the 2-year at 4.41%, and the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 4 September shows 4.37%, 4.78% and 5.24% across the 2-, 10- and 30-year constant maturities. That combination of rising energy costs and rising long yields into a CPI week, with a Federal Reserve decision on 16 September where consensus looks for a move to 4.00%, is a demanding environment but not a pathological price path. Sector evidence from the latest session is genuinely split: semiconductors were strong, with Intel up around 9% on a report of a roughly 10% processor price increase and an upgrade, AMD up 5.9% and Qualcomm and Arm both higher, while software fell and six of the eight tracked megacaps closed lower. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction and belongs in stress and confidence rather than in tail. The day's own catalysts are second-tier: MBA mortgage data at 11:00 UTC, ADP weekly employment at 12:15 UTC, a 17-week bill auction at 15:30 UTC, then the 10-year note auction and the Apple 'Surprise and Shine' keynote together at 17:00 UTC, with the API crude stock change at 20:30 UTC. The Tier-1 releases, PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, both fall outside this 24-hour window. Tail therefore sits at 7 and peaks conditionally at 12 across the U.S. cash open, never approaching the 25 block threshold on current evidence.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours the mapped state stayed EA_ON throughout, with tail between 5 and 15 and no reading approaching the block threshold. The single elevated print was 15 at 14:00 UTC on 8 September during a brief trend-down phase in the first full U.S. cash hour, and it reverted within that same hour as the cash index recovered to close mid-range at 29,507.70. One hour, 09:00 UTC on 8 September, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Stress climbed steadily from 67 to 76 as crude advanced through $100 on Gulf supply disruption and the 10-year held near a two-decade high, while confidence stayed in an 85-89 band because live price-path evidence remained available through the U.S. session and the overnight Globex hours. Dominant mode was mixed in 21 of the 23 available hours, with one trend-down and one normal print, which is consistent with a market carrying heavy macro stress while still delivering the two-sided price path that mean-reversion approaches require.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain no Tier-1 U.S. macro release; PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, fall outside the window. Conditional tail stays in a 7-12 band and never approaches the block threshold, peaking at 12 across the 13:30-15:00 UTC U.S. cash open where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the specific failure mode of concern. Secondary steps sit at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.80% yield coincides with the Apple keynote and is labelled event/whipsaw for two-sided reaction risk, and at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Stress holds in a 75-79 band because it is carried by Brent above $100, a 10-year close to its highest since October 2023, an unresolved Strait of Hormuz escalation and a Federal Reserve decision on 16 September rather than by observed price structure. Confidence decays from 88 to 74 across the horizon as observed price-path evidence gives way to projection, with the overnight Asian hours labelled normal on the expectation of thin, range-bound conditions.
